transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because things have been... difficult lately at work. I'm a teacher, and recently the district decided to put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, right on top of my regular teaching duties. 

I mean, I'm still getting through the day, but I just feel so wound up and discouraged. It's really not like me. And I've noticed I'm starting to put off things like lesson plans and emails—things I used to handle without a second thought. I just don't feel like myself right now.
Do you find that you are spending a significant amount of your day worrying about many different areas of your life, rather than just these specific work-related stressors?

No, not really. It's... it's pretty much just focused on work. I don't find myself worrying about my family or my health or, you know, other parts of my life. It really all just comes back to this new rollout and how I'm going to manage it all. If it weren't for that, I think I'd be completely fine.
When you think about this work situation, do you feel more down, sad, and hopeless, or do you feel more nervous, jittery, and on edge?

I'm not really sure how to separate them, to be honest. I don't think I feel completely hopeless, or... or jittery, really. It's mostly just what I mentioned earlier—I feel very wound up and discouraged by the whole thing. I guess I'm just overwhelmed by the workload, but I wouldn't say it's exactly one or the other.
When you feel this way, do you find that your physical symptoms, like muscle tension or restlessness, are more bothersome than your feelings of sadness or loss of interest?

I haven't really noticed much in the way of physical symptoms, to be honest. I don't think my muscles are particularly tense, and I wouldn't say I'm restless. And... well, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in things, either. I still enjoy my time at home and my life outside of the classroom. It's really just that mental feeling of being overwhelmed and bogged down when I have to deal with all this new school stuff. So I guess neither of those things are really bothering me.
When you are at work and thinking about these challenges, do you experience more of a sense of sadness or a sense of nervousness?

I think it's more nervousness, if I had to pick. I don't really feel sad about it... it's just this anxious feeling about getting everything done. Like I said, I'm just wound up about the new curriculum and whether I can handle the workload. I wouldn't call it sadness at all.
Do you feel that this nervousness and feeling of being 'wound up' is significantly greater than what most people would experience when faced with a new work requirement?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean... I haven't exactly asked the other teachers how they're handling it. I'd imagine anyone would be stressed having a whole new curriculum and all this extra workload dumped on them. 

So, I don't know if my reaction is worse than what most people would feel... it just feels like a lot for me to manage right now.
Are these feelings of being 'wound up' and overwhelmed causing you to struggle significantly in your daily life, such as missing deadlines or having trouble functioning at home or at work?

I wouldn't say I'm struggling significantly at home, and I'm still teaching my classes and getting through the day. But at work... well, I have noticed I'm slipping a bit with the administrative side. I've missed a couple of planning deadlines, or had to push them back, which isn't like me. And I've actually needed a few reminders from the other teachers for things I used to just handle automatically. So I guess it is affecting how I function, at least when it comes to keeping up with all the paperwork and planning.

Even though you mentioned you don't feel sad, do you find that you have less energy or motivation to do things, or perhaps that you have a more negative outlook on your future than you normally would?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I'm tired by the time the final bell rings, but that's pretty normal for teaching. I wouldn't say I have less energy or motivation overall. I still get up and do what I need to do at home and in the classroom. 

And... as for the future, no, I don't feel negative about it. I'm really just stressed about this immediate hurdle, you know? I figure once I finally get a grip on this new curriculum, things will go back to normal. So, no, I don't feel hopeless or anything like that.
Even though you don't feel hopeless, have you noticed that you are crying more often than usual or feeling emotionally numb?
No, neither of those. I haven't been crying at all, really. And I definitely don't feel numb... if anything, I just feel tense and keyed up about all the extra work. But no crying or feeling empty.
